# KataGo Remote One-Click v0.1.1

Adds an optional fixed hostname on your own Cloudflare domain. Quick tunnels stay the default, and existing installations keep working.

## Highlights

- **Fixed hostname with a named tunnel**: serve `wss://katago.ykrsama.org/katago/<private-token>` from a Cloudflare Tunnel token. The address survives service restarts, server reboots, and public IP changes.
  - `katago-remote init --tunnel-mode named --tunnel-hostname katago.example.org --tunnel-token-file /path/to/token`
  - The installer reads `KATAGO_REMOTE_TUNNEL_HOSTNAME` plus `KATAGO_REMOTE_TUNNEL_TOKEN` or `KATAGO_REMOTE_TUNNEL_TOKEN_FILE`.
  - The tunnel token is stored under `state/tunnel-token` with mode `600` and passed to cloudflared through `TUNNEL_TOKEN`, never through the process arguments.
- **Safer reconfiguration**: `init` now only overwrites the flags you pass, so switching tunnel modes keeps existing engine paths, listen address, and `maxVisits`.
- **Better diagnostics**: `doctor` reports the tunnel hostname, token, and the ingress target that the Cloudflare Public Hostname must use.
- **Go 1.27.4** toolchain, which fixes GO-2026-6859 in `net/http`.

## Upgrade

```bash
curl -fsSLo /tmp/katago-remote-install.sh \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ykrsama/katago-remote-one-click/v0.1.1/install.sh
bash /tmp/katago-remote-install.sh
```

Existing KataGo, model, and analysis config files are reused.

## Fixed hostname

Follow the [English guide](https://github.com/ykrsama/katago-remote-one-click/blob/v0.1.1/docs/FIXED-DOMAIN.md) or the [Chinese guide](https://github.com/ykrsama/katago-remote-one-click/blob/v0.1.1/docs/FIXED-DOMAIN.zh-CN.md). The tunnel must run on the GPU server; the private path token remains the only access control.
